The note is incorrect: Habermas’s distinction is not about media portrayals versus courts. "Law as medium" is formally rational steering law that coordinates the economic and administrative systems through money and power, while "law as institution" is lifeworld-rooted normative law (e.g., constitutional rights, family law) that depends on communicative justification and sustains solidarity. The distinction contrasts system-integrating instrumental law with lifeworld-protecting normative law.
CONFIDENCE: 95
